A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSAS research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, proofs and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data experiments, Bayesian-network evaluations, Cattaneo2 estimates and appendix sensitivity studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces zero-effect assignment followed by Break with immediate return of zero, changing the stated termination behavior. The MMB discovery procedure and R1/R2 selection logic remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same two synthetic structures, INSURANCE, MILDEW, WIN95PTS, ANDES and Cattaneo2. The pretreatment-violation and varying-latent-variable scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain PA, LV-IDA with RFCI, EHS and CEELS. Relocated benchmark tables preserve comparator membership, including timeout entries.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, data generation, regression estimation, RE and nTest metrics, the 0.01 conditional-independence test threshold and conditioning-set limits remain unchanged. Several settings move to Appendix E.

E4.justification: The MILDEW sensitivity studies on pretreatment-assumption violations and latent-variable counts move from v1 Appendix B to v2 Appendix E.1-E.2 with the same analyses and evidence.

E5.justification: Both report 100 repetitions with randomly generated data, averaged results with the same plus/minus reporting, and 95% confidence intervals for Cattaneo2. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All 32 empirical table rows match, and the real-data figure retains the same estimates and findings. For example, MILDEW at 10K retains LSAS RE 4.76% and nTest 60.87 in v1 Table V and v2 Table 4.

T1.justification: Several adjustment definitions narrow their domains from also covering CPDAGs/PAGs to DAGs/MAGs, and the within-blanket adjustment definition drops PAGs. The explicit no-selection-bias assumption is removed. The five main theorem statements and underlying proof strategies are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims: fully local covariate selection with latent variables, soundness and completeness under the stated assumptions, and empirical effectiveness.

C2.justification: v1 explicitly notes that selection bias can prevent identification using covariate adjustment; v2 omits this applicability qualification. The pretreatment and conditional-independence identifiability limitations are otherwise retained in Appendix F.

D1.justification: v2 Section 4 newly states that source code is included in supplementary materials; the supplied PDFs do not establish its actual availability. Hardware, hyperparameters and comparator access links are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: The Richardson and Spirtes (2002) citation and reference are removed. The remaining related-work discussion and positioning relative to prior methods are substantially unchanged, with related work relocated to Appendix A.

P1.justification: v2 extensively reorganizes the document: related work, detailed definitions, proofs, complexity analysis and limitations move into dedicated appendices. It also revises the conclusion, adds an Impact Statement, removes acknowledgments and updates the author list.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different conference layout and extensively redistributes existing displays. Visibility and MMB figures, notation/network tables, and INSURANCE/ANDES results move to appendices, while the algorithm-feature table moves into the method section. The underlying graphical evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: The streamlined organization and explicit zero-effect returns offer clarity gains, but v2 removes the selection-bias qualification. Its narrowed adjustment definitions also leave scope unclear when the retained Appendix D proofs invoke them for PAGs. With unchanged empirical evidence and supplementary-code availability unverified, these mixed effects do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
